correctionToMyOwnReport: I previously described 'three unattributed failures'. That was wrong and understated the surface. The full run is 6 failing FILES / 9 failing TESTS / 6333 passed / 16 skipped. All nine are classified below individually, with the evidence that decided each.
method: Each failing test is attributed by asking two questions with reproducible answers: (1) is the stylesheet or source it pins listed in R0/receipts/round-start-porcelain.txt, i.e. already dirty before this round; (2) is that path in the set R1 actually edited. A failure is MINE only when R1 edited the thing the assertion reads.

attributions.test: EmbeddedCssRecovery.contract.test.ts > pins every DataTable interaction selector and animation body
attributions.evidence: The pin covers seven stylesheets: data-table-interactions, form-placeholders, navigation-static, primitive-motion, scroll-area, tabs, toast-animation-keyframes. R1 edited NONE of them. data-table-interactions.css is listed in the round-start porcelain, so it was already modified before this round.

attributions.test: EmbeddedCssRecovery.contract.test.ts > pins all six audited stylesheets byte-for-byte
attributions.evidence: Same seven-stylesheet set, same disjointness from the R1 edit set.

attributions.test: Menu.modern-engine.test.tsx > owns the 62/45 level geometry against the legacy sidebar bridge
attributions.evidence: menu.css is listed in the round-start porcelain and R1 never edited it. It appears in `git status` only because it was already dirty.

attributions.test: Spinner.modern-engine.test.tsx > keeps ring geometry, cadence and the reduced-motion guard in the skin
attributions.evidence: spinner.css IS in the round-start porcelain at line 73 (an earlier check of mine reported it clean; that check was malformed and the porcelain is authoritative). The failing assertion is the --ds-motion-slow duration pin, which the 2026-08-03 inherited change superseded. R1 edits to this file were the track-colour rebase and the :root token rebase, neither of which touches the duration expression. Count held at 1 failed / 22 passed before and after both edits.
Present in the original four-failure compiler baseline captured before any Cohort 1 write.

attributions.test: premium-regression.test.ts > bithire generates input vars with correct values
attributions.evidence: The assertion is `expect(css).toContain('--ds-input-bg: #ffffff')`. R1 rebased BitHire's chrome.controls.input.bg from the literal "#ffffff" to "var(--ds-surface-inset, #ffffff)", so the generated artifact now emits the var() chain instead of the literal. This is the one failure in the run attributable to this round.
attributions.isTheChangeCorrect: Yes. It is what made field chrome tenant-reachable: --ds-input-border and --ds-input-border-focus were byte-identical across both tenants before it, and now diverge (rgb(215,226,234) cool vs rgb(201,195,182) warm). The pin is also correct — it was protecting a real contract. Both are right, which is why this needs adjudication rather than a unilateral edit.

attributions.test: canonical-digest-identity.test.ts > produces one digest for a document authored in any key order
attributions.evidence: Corrected by independent audit. R0 records exactly these three reds, caused by the INHERITED removal of --ds-motion-ambient. My own cohort-1-schema-digest-proof.json independently confirms artifactDigestsUntouched, and R1 moved none of the six artifact pins. My earlier "compounded by R1" framing was wrong in the cautious direction — I hedged toward claiming more responsibility than the evidence supports, which is still a misattribution.
